title: Group Odd and Even Positions

concept.title: Two chains built in one walk
body: Put all nodes at **odd positions** (1st, 3rd, 5th, ...) first, followed by all nodes at **even positions** (2nd, 4th, ...), keeping the order inside both groups. The positions count from 1 and are about the **place** in the list, not about the value.

Use two references, `odd` and `even`, both advancing by **two** nodes in each step and relinking as they go: the odd chain skips the even node, the even chain skips the odd node. Remember the head of the even chain (`even_head`) because at the end the odd chain has to be connected to it.

body.code:
odd, even = head, head.next
even_head = even
while even is not None and even.next is not None:
    odd.next = even.next;  odd = odd.next
    even.next = odd.next;  even = even.next
odd.next = even_head

body: The pointers are changed in place, so no extra memory is needed. An empty list has nothing to do.

statement: Rearrange a singly linked list: first all nodes at odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, ...) and then all nodes at even positions (2nd, 4th, ...), each group in its original order. Print the new list.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of nodes. The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail.
outputFormat: Print the values of the new list on one line.

examples.note: The 1st, 3rd and 5th nodes (1 3 5) come first, then 2 4: 1 3 5 2 4.

hints: Keep two references: the last node of the odd chain and the last node of the even chain.
In every step, `odd` links to the node after `even`, then `even` links to the node after the new `odd`.
Save the head of the even chain and attach it behind the odd chain at the end.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(odd_even_list(build_list(a)))

explanation: The odd and the even chain are built at the same time by relinking two nodes per step; the head of the even chain is attached behind the odd chain at the end.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))


def odd_even_list(head):
    if head is None:
        return head
    odd = head
    even = head.next
    even_head = even
    while even is not None and even.next is not None:
        odd.next = even.next
        odd = odd.next
        even.next = odd.next
        even = even.next
    odd.next = even_head
    return head

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(odd_even_list(build_list(a)))
free_nodes()
